jobs.title: Senior Director, Radar Technical Program Management
jobs.excerpt: Why LeoLabs? At LeoLabs, we’re building the living map of activity in space.
jobs.description:
Why LeoLabs?

At LeoLabs, we’re building the living map of activity in space. Through our proprietary global radar network and AI-enabled analytics platform, we collect millions of measurements daily on more than 25,000 objects in low Earth orbit (LEO). Our radar-powered intelligence protects billions in assets, monitors adversarial behavior, and ensures safe operations for commercial and government missions.

We’re not just building technology, we are redefining global security, safety, and transparency in space. As orbital activity accelerates and threats grow more complex, LeoLabs is a trusted partner for Space Domain Awareness, Space Traffic Management, and Satellite Operations for top-tier space operators and allied defense organizations.

If you're looking to work on mission-critical challenges at the forefront of aerospace, national security, and AI, your impact starts here.

LeoLabs is seeking a Senior Director, Radar Technical Program Management to lead the integrated technical execution of our most complex radar, hardware, production, and infrastructure programs.

This role is a senior technical leadership role responsible for coalescing the entire Radar organization around a single, credible execution plan which will be visible across the enterprise. The role operates across the Radar organization, spanning radar systems engineering, RF and electromechanical engineering, software and embedded systems, supply chain, manufacturing, EHS, site development, integration, test, operations, and maintenance.

You will also partner closely with Product, customer-facing Program Management, Finance, and other cross-functional teams. You will translate product objectives and customer commitments into credible engineering plans, identify system-level dependencies, resolve blockers, and own the integrated execution plan of record from development through operational deployment.

You will initially lead several high-priority initiatives and, as the portfolio grows, build and lead a small team of technically credible program leaders.

Success in this role requires technical depth, engineering judgment, systems thinking, practical hardware-development experience, and the ability to engage credibly with senior engineers while driving complex programs to measurable outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Lead Complex Technical Programs

  • Lead multidisciplinary radar, hardware, manufacturing, deployment, and operational-readiness programs from definition through completion.
  • Translate product requirements, technical objectives, customer commitments, and operational needs into program definitions with clear scope, success criteria, major milestones, interfaces, dependencies, and decision points.
  • Drive execution through ambiguity, evolving requirements, incomplete information, and aggressive schedules while maintaining accountability for overall program outcomes.

Own the Radar Program Plan of Record

  • Coordinate execution across Radar Systems, Hardware Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Global Infrastructure, Radar Operations, Product, and customer-facing Program Management.
  • Own the integrated technical program baseline and cross-functional commitments for scope, schedule, cost, readiness, and risk. Establish change control and drive escalation and recovery, and ensure decisions are made by appropriate functional authority. Product retains roadmap and prioritization authority while engineering leaders retain technical design authority.
  • Build schedules that reflect engineering maturity, critical paths, long-lead materials, supplier and site dependencies, resource contention, and schedule risk.
  • Assess the downstream schedule and resource effects of architecture changes, component substitutions, test failures, supplier delays, and scope changes, and update the plan of record accordingly.

Lead Technical Readiness, Risk, and Change Management

  • Define and lead technical and deployment readiness reviews across the product lifecycle, from requirements and architecture through design release, prototype builds, verification and validation, product readiness, site integration, acceptance, and operational handoff.
  • Establish entry and exit criteria and ensure reviews evaluate technical and deployment maturity, test evidence, configuration status, documentation, and residual risk.
  • Partner with the responsible engineers and functional leaders to ensure technical decisions and changes are evidence-based and made by the appropriate authority.
  • Manage technical risks, issues, assumptions, dependencies, changes, and decisions; surface material problems early and drive root-cause analysis and recovery planning.
  • Partner with customer-facing Program Management to maintain traceability from contractual milestones and customer acceptance criteria to technical baselines, verification requirements and evidence, and executable delivery plans.

Support Prototype Development, Production, and Deployment

  • Coordinate the transition of radar and hardware products from engineering development into repeatable production.
  • Integrate design release, materials, DfX, tooling, test equipment, calibration, quality, labor, capacity, yield, and cost targets into credible production plans.
  • Partner with Supply Chain to incorporate supplier capability, lead times, material availability, obsolescence, and alternate-source readiness into program schedules and risk assessments.
  • Coordinate technical resolution of issues discovered during prototype, pilot, and production builds, and incorporate lessons into subsequent design and program baselines.
  • Integrate site development, regulatory dependencies, logistics, installation, system integration, acceptance testing, and operational readiness into deployment schedules.
  • Define clear handoff criteria for Radar Operations and Maintenance teams and establish feedback loops that inform sustaining-engineering priorities.

Provide Technical Program Leadership

  • Provide concise, forward-looking program reviews to the SVP and other members of LeoLabs’ extended leadership team, including milestone confidence, critical-path changes, key dependencies, resource conflicts, and recovery options.
  • Present the technical, schedule, cost, and operational consequences of major decisions and identify the decision or support required from leadership.
  • Maintain a portfolio-level view of major milestones, dependencies, risks, and capacity constraints.
  • Partner with Radar team business operations and FP&A to connect scope and schedule changes to budget, cost, and margin impacts.
  • Ensure external commitments are backed by credible technical execution plans.
  • Build and lead a scalable technical program management function that enables engineering and functional leaders to focus on technical quality, organization capacity, and functional execution.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a technically credible, detail-oriented program leader who has operated at the intersection of engineering, hardware development, manufacturing, and deployment. You bring enough technical depth to challenge assumptions and understand system-level tradeoffs, combined with the organizational judgement to drive execution across teams without direct authority. You are comfortable operating at both the executive and engineering levels and know how to turn ambiguity into clear decisions, accountable plans, and measurable outcomes.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, physics, computer science, or another relevant technical discipline, or equivalent technical experience.
  • 12+ years of experience in engineering, systems engineering, technical program management, hardware program leadership, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated success leading multidisciplinary systems from concept through development, prototype builds, verification, production readiness, integration, deployment, and operational use.
  • Experience with complex electronic, RF, or electromechanical systems in aerospace, defense, space, telecommunications, or another hardware-intensive environment.
  • Strong understanding of requirements, interfaces, architecture, verification, validation, configuration, and technical risk.
  • Experience integrating hardware, software, manufacturing, supply chain, test, infrastructure, and operational workstreams.
  • Experience building integrated engineering plans and managing milestones, critical paths, assumptions, resource constraints, and recovery plans.
  • Ability to challenge technical assumptions and influence senior engineering leaders.
  • Exceptional written, verbal, and executive communication skills.
  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. personnel security clearance and satisfy applicable U.S. export-control requirements.
  • Experience managing international infrastructure, permitting, spectrum, regulatory, or site-acceptance dependencies.
  • Familiarity with requirements-management, PLM, ERP, scheduling, and engineering-work-management systems.
  • Experience leading, mentoring, and developing technical program managers or other cross-functional program leaders, with the ability to build scalable program-management practices.

What Success Looks Like

  • Within 30 days, you will develop a working understanding of LeoLabs’ radar systems, active programs, deployments, and operating models, and begin leading one or two priority programs.
  • Within 90 days, you will establish integrated plans for priority initiatives, create visibility into milestones and critical paths, implement a decision-oriented program review, and introduce practical readiness and risk-management practices.
  • Within six months, you will improve coordination across engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, infrastructure, deployment, and operations; establish credible baselines and forecasts; and build appropriate TPM coverage for priority programs.
  • Within twelve months, you will own and operate a trusted technical program-management capability supporting radar products, commercial hardware, research and development, production, deployment, and sustaining initiatives. Functional leaders will spend less time acting as de facto project managers. LeoLabs leadership will have a credible view of the Radar organization’s full technical execution schedule, risks, and resource constraints.

The base salary range for this position is $$230,000-$250,000 + bonus + stock options + benefits 

Compensation Note: The salary range for this position is benchmarked based on the designated primary work location for the role. Final compensation may vary depending on the selected candidate's work location, applicable market data, experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors.

ITAR Requirements

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. More information regarding ITAR can be found at DDTC’s website

  • Collaboration 🤝 – Together, we achieve more.
  • Growth 🌱 – We’re committed to personal and professional development.

At Hi Rasmus, we trust our team to do great work, their way. Flexibility, autonomy, and balance are key—we know that when life and work fit together, everyone thrives. 🏡✨
  • Flat structure, open doors – Every voice matters. Collaboration and shared decision-making drive us forward.
  • Balance is a priority – Recharge, make time for what matters, and do your best work in a way that works for you.
  • Real impact, real growth – Be part of a team making a difference for families worldwide, while growing your skills along the way.

Join us in shaping a future where exceptional autism care is within reach for all. 💡💙

📢 About the Role

💼 Job Title: Principal Software Engineer
📍 Location: Fully remote within Europe (CET ±2 hours)
⏳ Job Type: Full-time
⭐️ Reports to: Director of Engineering
💰 Compensation: 67-72,000 DKK / month

🧑‍💻 About You

We are looking for a deeply hands-on Principal Software Engineer to be the most senior technical individual contributor at Hi Rasmus. Reporting to our Director of Engineering, this is a role on our Principal track, a craft career path that sits alongside the management track rather than beneath it.

Where a Lead Software Engineer is the strongest technical contributor within one outcome team, the Principal Software Engineer works across all of them. You will help shape and evolve our platform architecture, strengthen shared technical practices, mentor Senior and Lead Engineers, and take on complex challenges that span teams or domains.

This is not an advisory role. You will work alongside teams in the code, helping solve difficult problems and piloting new tools, patterns, and practices through real work. Your goal is not to become a permanent escalation point, but to leave teams more capable of making strong technical decisions independently.

You lead through technical judgement, architecture, code review, collaboration and example rather than through reporting lines. Software Engineers sit in the outcome teams and report to their Lead Engineer. You will provide technical guidance and mentorship across teams, while people leadership, performance management, staffing and overall Engineering accountability remain with Lead Engineers and the Director of Engineering. As we scale, we are relying increasingly on AI and automation to improve engineering leverage. Working in partnership with the Director of Engineering and CTO, you will help translate our company and Engineering direction into sound architecture, modern technical practices, and durable internal capability.

📌What You’ll Do

  • Work alongside outcome teams to solve complex technical problems, particularly those spanning systems, teams, or domains.
  • Pilot new tools, patterns, and practices through real production work before supporting broader adoption.
  • Facilitate the architecture forum, bringing Product and other stakeholders into decisions early and establishing a clear process for documenting, communicating, and revisiting those decisions.
  • Partner with the Director of Engineering, CTO, and Lead Engineers to guide the evolution of our web and mobile platform across Vue 3, Quasar, Capacitor, Node.js, Firebase, Firestore, and Google Cloud Platform.
  • Evaluate and recommend tooling and framework decisions, including build, buy, adopt, or retire recommendations grounded in real evidence and business needs.
  • Take on the complex, cross-cutting problems that span teams or that no single team can own, and land them in production.
  • Establish shared technical standards across code quality, testing, APIs, data modelling, documentation, and system design, building adoption through practical value, review, and example.
  • Surface technical debt, performance, scalability, and system-health risks early, and partner with Engineering leadership to prioritize the right investments.
  • Strengthen internal ownership of critical systems, architectural decisions, deployment paths, and operational knowledge through clear documentation, knowledge-sharing, and hands-on collaboration.
  • Build alignment across teams through the Lead Engineers guild while preserving the ownership and autonomy of individual outcome teams.
  • Advance responsible AI-assisted development practices and evaluate their impact on quality, speed, reliability, privacy, and security. Help scale what works and thoughtfully retire practices that no longer serve us.
  • Identify technical risk, performance, and scalability problems before they are urgent, and lead the work to remove them.
  • Mentor Senior and Lead Engineers through pairing, design review, technical feedback, and shared problem-solving.
  • Contribute to the engineering career ladder and to levelling and calibration, and act as the technical assessor in engineering hiring, with decisions owned by Lead Engineers and the Director of Engineering.
  • Partner with the Principal QA Engineer, Product, and DevOps so that quality, testability, and operability are designed in rather than added later.
  • Contribute to compliance and audit readiness by helping make sure our technical practices hold up to external scrutiny in a regulated healthcare context.

🌱 What Success Looks LikeWithin your first 6–12 months:
  • Teams are using a shared, practical architecture decision process, with important decisions clearly documented and understood.
  • Ownership of critical domains and systems is clearer, and the highest-priority cross-team technical risks and debt have actionable plans.
  • AI-assisted development practices are producing measurable improvements without compromising quality, privacy, security, or reliability.
  • Senior and Lead Engineers are more confident making complex technical decisions, with fewer issues requiring escalation.
  • Critical platform and operational knowledge is increasingly shared, documented, and owned internally.

🎯What You Bring

  • Extensive experience as a Senior, Lead, or Principal Software Engineer, with a track record of delivering complex, production-grade systems.
  • Deep technical capability that remains current. You can step into a difficult problem, contribute meaningfully in the code, and help carry the solution into production.
  • Deep proficiency in Vue 3 and Node.js, with strong full-stack understanding.
  • Strong, practical experience with Domain-Driven Design. You can identify bounded contexts within a complex domain, model them thoughtfully, and protect those boundaries under delivery pressure. Experience applying tactical DDD in code is essential.
  • Solid experience with Firebase, Firestore, and Google Cloud Platform services.
  • A track record of setting technical direction across multiple teams, not just delivering within one.
  • Deep architecture experience across approaches such as layered systems, event-driven architecture, and modular monoliths, with the judgment to choose appropriate patterns and explain trade-offs clearly.
  • A track record of influencing technical direction across multiple teams, not only delivering within one.
  • The ability to connect architecture and technical trade-offs to product goals, customer needs, business outcomes, and responsible growth.
  • High code-quality standards and strong opinions, held with curiosity and openness.
  • The ability to build adoption through credibility, usefulness, and collaboration rather than authority.
  • Clear written communication, particularly through design documents, architectural decision records, standards, and thoughtful review feedback.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity, navigating disagreement constructively, and making sound decisions when there is no perfect answer.
  • Strong interest in AI-assisted development and modern engineering workflows.
  • Experience working in an empowered product-team model, such as the approach described in Marty Cagan’s INSPIRED, is a plus.
  • Experience in healthcare, regulated technology, or another environment where privacy, security, quality, and trust matter deeply is also a plus.
We know that great candidates may not meet every qualification listed. If this role excites you and you believe your experience could help us grow, we encourage you to apply.

💙 Perks & Benefits You'll Love

🎓 Growth & Development:
  • Professional development opportunities
  • Room for growth within the company
🏡 Work Style That Works for You:
  • Fully remote and flexible work environment—work from wherever feels right!
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful impact in the Autism healthcare space

📩 How to Apply

Use our applicant tracking system Pinpoint to answer the role-specific application questions. These questions were thoughtfully designed to give you more insight into the role and to give us more insight into you. Please write a thoughtful response—a human really reads these.
If you need accommodations during the application process, just let us know—we’re happy to help. 😊

jobs.description:
About Kalepa:

Insurance is a $7T global industry built on professional labor: underwriting, claims, pricing, operations, and distribution. Kalepa is building AI that can perform that work.

We create professional-grade AI systems for insurers: software that can read, reason, decide, and act inside real workflows and operate over long-time horizons. Kalepa begins by augmenting professionals with the tools to succeed at their jobs. That earns us the right to learn from real decisions, capture decision traces, and automate what can be automated successfully over time.

Our products are already in production with leading insurers, driving measurable outcomes and expanding across functions. The opportunity is far broader than any single workflow: to build the AI operating system for decision-making across insurance. For people who want to work on AI that matters, in a sector where correctness, trust, and real-world impact count, Kalepa is just getting started.

Kalepa is backed by leading investors such as IA Ventures and Inspired Capital, and our team brings experience from Facebook, Palantir, Google, Amazon, McKinsey, Mastercard, and Uber.

Our Values (This is important):

Many organizations have a dusty list of corporate values that no one ever follows. Kalepa is not one of those companies. Our values are designed to unlock the potential of our employees.

Success at Kalepa is bred from five core principles:

  • Hustle and Determination - We hire people who take full ownership of their craft and relentlessly pursue excellence with speed and determination. We choose the hard problems and do not give up. This is the foundation of how we work and how we win.
  • Deliver Customer Impact - We're obsessed with customer impact. Every feature, every line of code, every decision is measured against one question: does this help insurers make better decisions? If it doesn't drive speed, accuracy, or profitability for our customers, we don't build it.
  • Meritocracy - We're building something exceptional, and that requires exceptional people and ideas. We have a high bar but we reward excellence with rapid growth. If you're the best at what you do, you'll thrive here.
  • Transparency - We value honest, transparent communication over politics. We challenge ideas, not people. We say what needs to be said, even when it's hard. This is how we solve problems fast and find the truth.
  • Experiment Relentlessly - Many of the problems we face have never been solved before. We tackle them by testing quickly, measuring rigorously, and iterating until we find the path forward. Speed of learning is our advantage.

In addition to our NY office, we have remote employees speaking 10+ languages across the globe. But we invest in bringing our people together both for regional meetups and global offsites (2021 - Playa Del Carmen | 2022 - Rome | 2023 - Buenos Aires | 2024 - Lisbon | 2025 - Cartagena).

Kalepa’s culture isn’t for everyone, and that’s ok. But for the people who are a fit, they can’t imagine working elsewhere.

About the role:

Salary range: $85K - $135K USD*

Location: USA (Remote)

Kalepa is looking for an exceptional Technical Support Engineer with 3-5 years of experience in B2B SaaS technical support, customer-facing engineering, or a similar customer-facing technical role to be a critical member of our Support organization. This role is designed to own the technical investigation and resolution of issues across Kalepa's AI platform for insurance.

You'll be the connective tissue between our customers and our development teams, triaging and investigating complex technical issues, driving resolutions, and building the systems and processes that make our support function world-class. You'll work directly with large-scale enterprise clients who rely on Kalepa's platform to make critical decisions, so your ability to earn trust, communicate clearly under pressure, and go deep on technical problems is critical.

What you'll do:

Technical Investigation & Resolution

  • Investigate reported issues end to end within Kalepa’s AI underwriting platform. Coordinate technical resolution end-to-end.
  • Distinguish working-as-expected behavior from genuine bugs, configuration issues, user education gaps, and feature requests.
  • Manage your own queue and hit response and resolution targets consistently.

Client Communication

  • Draft responses to Kalepa’s clients that are clear, accurate, and resolve the issue without unnecessary back and forth.
  • Maintain professional, consistent communication across all client touchpoints.

Engineering & Cross-Functional Coordination

  • File Jira tickets with full diagnostic context when issues are confirmed bugs, so Engineering has what they need to resolve quickly.
  • Identify patterns across tickets and surface them to Client Success and Product as themes worth addressing structurally.

Product & Subject Matter Expertise

  • Become an expert user of Kalepa, with deep familiarity across workflows, edge cases, and product behavior. Build and maintain per-client implementation knowledge.

About you:

  • Experience at a high-growth tech startup.
  • You have 3-5 years of experience in a Technical Support Engineer, Senior Technical Solutions Specialist, or similar customer-facing technical role at a B2B SaaS company.
  • You communicate clearly in writing. You can explain technical issues to non-technical audiences and write responses that hold up under scrutiny from sophisticated users.
  • You are comfortable operating in ambiguity. Many of the issues you will own do not have a documented answer, and the right resolution requires synthesizing product behavior, client context, and operational judgment.
  • You are operationally disciplined. You manage your own queue, hit response targets consistently, and do not let things age.
  • You are metrics-driven, with a strong ability to combine quantitative and qualitative insights.
  • You value open, direct, and respectful communication.
  • You enjoy being part of a collaborative, thoughtful, and purpose-driven environment.
  • Experience supporting complex data-heavy SaaS products

As a plus:

  • Insurtech or Fintech product experience.

What you’ll get

  • Competitive salary (based on experience level).
  • Significant equity options package.
  • 401(k) plan with employer match (regardless of employee contribution)
  • Excellent benefits: 100% covered medical, 100% covered vision and dental for individuals and families, and others
  • Work with an ambitious, smart, global, and fun team to transform a $1T global industry.
  • 20 days of PTO a year
  • Global team offsites (2021 - Playa del Carmen, 2022 - Rome, 2023 - Buenos Aires, 2024 - Lisbon, 2025 - Cartagena)
  • Healthy living/gym stipend. Mobile phone bill stipend.
  • Continuing education credits.

*The salary range listed is an estimate and will vary based on a variety of factors. Final compensation will be determined during the offer stage based on relevant experience, performance during the interview process, and geographic location, and may therefore differ from the posted range.

jobs.description:
Mission - Why we exist, what we do, and why we need you

Onomi is the HCP engagement and intelligence platform for life sciences. Pharma commercial and medical teams use Onomi to run their HCP engagements, congresses, webinars, advisory boards, and everyday meetings, and to capture what actually happens in them: every interaction captured with consent, matched to the right HCP record, and written back to Veeva or Salesforce in minutes, so the engagement they already pay for comes back as data their teams can act on.

Why now:

This is Onomi's first dedicated business development role in the US, and you are not starting from zero. We have a strong US account management and event services team on the ground, a US customer base of 100 referenceable pharma companies including AstraZeneca, Takeda, Sanofi, GSK, and BeOne, and over 500,000 HCPs engaged across our platform every month. Our go-to-market is event-first: our leadership team speaks at the industry's events, usually with a booth alongside, and you will be there with them; at key conventions we prospect as participants, where our customers gather; our biweekly webinars hand you a warm, named audience after every session. What has been missing are the people on the ground converting that presence and proof into new logos. We are hiring 3 talents at once as our founding US new-business group, working directly with the CEO, the leadership team, and senior sales colleagues in other regions.

What you will do:

  • [35%] Work industry events: build target lists from attendee data before each event, staff the booth at leadership's speaking events, prospect conventions as a participant (first alongside colleagues, then solo), and follow up with every named contact with relevant messaging.
  • [20%] Run personalized outbound to webinar audiences and industry event attendee lists, turning warm names into booked first meetings. No mass sequences; every message is yours and very specific.
  • [20%] Run first meetings: your three-slide story, sharp discovery questions, and a crisp follow-up that gets forwarded internally.
  • [25%] Progress opportunities with senior support: bring in a senior seller, our solutions team or our leadership team at the right moment, keep every deal moving in an open deal channel, and co-sell through scoping and close.

What we need from you:

In your first month, you will:

  • Join our leadership team at live industry events: staff the booth at tradeshows and walk congresses with them.
  • Master our core sales plays: rehearse them, listen to past winning calls, and run mock first meetings that convince the team you can do it alone.
  • Start outbound on your first event attendee list and webinar audience, and book your first attended meetings.

In your first 3 months, you will:

  • Have 30+ attended first meetings on the board, with a 70%-plus show rate.
  • Staff your first medical convention solo, with a pre-event target list, a floor contact log, and 100% follow-up.
  • Convert each webinar cycle into at least 2 attended meetings.
  • Have your first opportunities in discovery with a senior co-seller attached.

By month 6, you will have closed your first new US logo, co-sold with a senior colleague (for which you will get 100% quota retirement), and earned a clear conversation about your lane: toward closing bigger deals or leading meeting generation as we scale the team.

What you need to be great at:

  • Speed and consistency despite ambiguity: following up same day, never dropping a ball, staying creative when the playbook runs out.
  • Curiosity about the product and the customer: you ask why a customer runs things the way they do, you go into the layers underneath.
  • Nobody expects you to become a sales engineer, but if your answer to every product question is 'let me loop someone in,' buyers lose interest and the someone loses patience.
  • In-person presence: you are at your best on a floor, at a booth, in a hallway conversation, and you want to travel to make that happen (expect to hop on a plane every 2-3 weeks).
  • Taking feedback fast: we coach constantly; what we correct on Monday shows up in your work on Tuesday.
  • Working with support rather than an army: you handle what you can and escalate deliberately.
  • Writing that sells: short, specific, personal messages that get replies.

What we are most curious about:

  • Tell us about events or trade shows you have worked on: what you did before, on, and after the floor, and what it produced, with real numbers.
  • Walk us through a product you sold and what sat underneath it: how it worked, why customers chose it, what its limits were.
  • What are 2 or 3 outreach tactics that reliably got you replies and meetings, and how did you know they worked?
  • Tell us about the last piece of feedback that changed how you work, and what changed.

Compensation: 150,000 to 190,000 USD on-target earnings (60% base, 40% variable), with guaranteed variable during ramp.

US-based, remote, near a major hub airport.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

YOUR MINDSET
You have spent your career becoming fluent in disciplines most people keep separate. You don't see creative strategy and media strategy as different languages. You see them as different expressions of the same strategic thinking. That mastery is what qualifies you for this role.

You believe that the best ideas scale, that coherence matters more than novelty, and that the team creating the strategy is as important as the strategy itself. You lead with conviction and curiosity. You build a culture where people think bigger about their work because they get excited about it.

ROLE OVERVIEW
You will help imagine, architect and operate an Intelligent Story System for a multi-brand healthcare enterprise at the executive level, setting the vision that orchestrates three interconnected business units - consumer retail operations, pharmacy benefit management, and health insurance - ensuring every strategic decision, creative expression, and media deployment radiates from a powerful idea.

This leadership role demands mastery of two disciplines that most separate: Brand Strategy and Connected Strategy. You have spent your career developing deep expertise in both. You don't translate between them. You hold them as one integrated practice.

You lead the creation of Catalyzing Ideas. You orchestrate their deployment. You're persuasive in the C-suite. You grow their business and that strengthens our relationship. You develop the next generation of integrated leaders. You are the strategic authority on how three interconnected brands move as one. You will report to the Chief Strategy Officer.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Boldness - Ideas

  • Shape and create the Catalyzing Idea(s) that will help orchestrate across three distinct business units with sophistication and specificity
  • A builder of brand worlds that dimensionalize ideas- articulating character, conviction, and edges with rigor and specificity that drives great creative work
  • Develop the strategic narratives that help enterprise leadership understand not just what you're doing, but why it matters and how it moves their business
  • Bring the same strategic depth to idea development as to system deployment. The ideas are the work. They are not secondary to execution, and brave ideas matter.

System Orchestration - The Deployment

  • Architect an Intelligent Story System: defining WHERE ideas reach the right audiences across all three business units and orchestrating HOW they show up in context
  • Identify audience signals that inform where and when each idea becomes urgent and inevitable
  • Ensure that as the system expands across channels, moments, and audiences, coherence never breaks. Every execution- whether retail media, pharmacy communications, or insurance education- radiates from the same idea
  • Lead creative, media, product, and retail teams to rally around the idea itself, not fracture into tactics. Help them understand they're part of something bigger than their discipline, and why their piece matters to the whole.

Cross-Brand Enterprise Leadership

  • Hold the enterprise perspective. You are the leader who sees where all three brands can move together and where they must move independently
  • Identify strategic opportunities where one idea scales across all three business units (creating compounding effect) and where each business unit needs its own force (creating specificity)
  • Create conditions where the three brands strengthen each other, not cannibalize each other

Media + Creative Integration at Strategic Foundation

  • Think in both languages simultaneously, from idea through deployment. You are fluent in creative strategy AND media strategy- not choosing between them, but weaving them together around an idea
  • You understand how media strategy informs which ideas can scale, which audiences you can reach, where cultural moments live. You understand how creative strategy demands certain media contexts to land. You hold both truths at once
  • Brief media and creative leaders not as separate functions receiving strategy, but as strategic partners who help shape how ideas move in the world

Relationship Growth & C-Suite Stewardship

  • Build and steward a mission-critical relationship by delivering integrated work that creates visible business impact for enterprise leadership
  • Position yourself as the strategic authority the enterprise turns to when the question is "how do our brands behave?" or "what's the opportunity we're missing?"
  • Create the conditions where integrated strategy becomes not a nice-to-have, but fundamental to how their enterprise operates

Team Building & Leadership Development

  • Help assemble and lead a world-class team that embodies integrated thinking at every level
  • Recruit for depth, not just breadth. You want strategists who are genuinely fluent in both creative and media thinking, not people who dabble in both
  • Develop the next generation of strategists who understand systems thinking, not just tactical execution
  • Create psychological safety where team members are empowered to challenge siloed thinking and contribute strategic ideas, not just execute briefs
  • A servant leader. Your actions help create our culture

Measurement, Learning & System Optimization

  • Create a learning agenda that tracks whether the system is actually working. Use measurement not as reporting, but as feedback. Let data inform how you tune the system for the next cycle

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

  • Your ideas are clear enough that a junior strategist can explain them. They're sophisticated enough that a CEO pauses and says "yes, that's what we're trying to do."
  • Creative and media strategies are inseparable. You cannot explain one without the other. The team describes them as one thing
  • All three business units operate from shared ethos while maintaining distinct expressions where it makes sense. The coherence is visible; the differentiation is clear
  • Your team thinks in systems. They understand signal stacking. They see how their work feeds the whole. New team members are onboarded into a way of thinking, not just a project
  • You have recruited and developed strategists who will lead integrated thinking across the agency- your legacy is multiplication
  • Measurement shows that ideas are proliferating, signals are clustering as predicted, and the system is compounding over time
  • The relationship grows because integrated strategy has become indispensable to how they operate. They ask for more

KEY QUALIFICATIONS

Experience:

  • 13+ years strategy experience with deep expertise in BOTH creative strategy AND media strategy
  • Demonstrated mastery of both disciplines - not sequential experience, but genuine fluency in how ideas and media interact
  • Proven track record defining strategic ideas, not just executing them
  • Leadership experience building and developing teams
  • Enterprise-level relationship management; comfort briefing C-suite

Intellectual Foundation:

  • Deep understanding of how systems work- not just campaigns, but interconnected strategic systems
  • Comfort holding complexity: three brands, multiple audiences, multiple signals, one coherent force
  • Ability to operate at 30,000-foot strategic level AND in the work itself
  • Evidence that you think about how ideas propagate and compound, not just how they perform in a single moment
